claim: check_env_gate_in_diff.py exists to block a new default-off *_ENABLED/*_DISABLED/MONITOR_* gate landing in a protected runtime path -- CLAUDE.md names this "the pattern that stranded MES." Its _PROTECTED_PREFIXES (lines 55-59) is ("src/runtime/", "src/units/", "src/web/") -- it omits src/core/ (home of coordinator.py, which CLAUDE.md itself names as the fold point for mode/execution gate resolution in Coordinator.multi_account_execute) and src/main.py (the entrypoint that calls run_pairs_tick, the isolated M22 pairs order path).
evidence: Constructed a synthetic diff adding `PAIRS_TRADING_ENABLED = os.environ.get("PAIRS_TRADING_ENABLED", "false")` to src/core/coordinator.py -> `env_gate_in_diff: clean (no offending changes)`, exit 0. Identical line added to src/main.py -> also clean, exit 0. The same line added to src/units/strategies/foo.py correctly tripped the guard (exit 1), confirming the pattern-matching logic itself works and only the path scope is the gap.
expected: A new default-off env-gate flag anywhere in the execution-critical path (including the coordinator's fold point and the main entrypoint) should trip the guard.
actual: The two most execution-critical files in the repo (per CLAUDE.md's own description of them) are outside the guard's protected-prefix set and a new stranding-shaped flag there passes silently.

detector: Extend the guard's own test suite with a case planting a new *_ENABLED line in src/core/coordinator.py and src/main.py and asserting the guard fires.
proposed_fix: Add "src/core/" and "src/main.py" to _PROTECTED_PREFIXES (or protected-files) in scripts/check_env_gate_in_diff.py.

claim: check_canonical_config_loaders.py exists to forbid a new hand-rolled yaml.safe_load parser of config/accounts.yaml outside the two allowlisted canonical readers -- the class of bug behind the 2026-05-16 backfill incident. _gather_offenders() (lines 112-135) only inspects yaml.safe_load calls found while walking FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef bodies (_scan_function, invoked only from a `for node in ast.walk(tree): if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))` loop) -- a yaml.safe_load call at module top-level (outside any function) is never visited.
evidence: python3 scripts/check_canonical_config_loaders.py --list on the clean repo -> "0 hand-rolled offenders." Planted a throwaway scripts/_tmp_hand_rolled_test.py with a top-level (non-function) yaml.safe_load(open("config/accounts.yaml")) call, re-ran the guard -> still "0 hand-rolled offenders" (file removed after the test; nothing committed to the repo).
expected: Any hand-rolled parser of config/accounts.yaml outside the two canonical readers should be flagged, regardless of whether it sits inside a function or at module scope.
actual: A brand-new top-level ops script (a very common shape in this repo's scripts/ tree) with a module-scope accounts.yaml parser is completely invisible to the guard.
population: 1 planted repro (module-level parser, not committed); the guard's own AST walk is restricted to 2 node types (FunctionDef, AsyncFunctionDef) repo-wide.
detector: Unit test: a fixture file with a module-level (not function-scoped) yaml.safe_load of config/accounts.yaml must be flagged as an offender.
proposed_fix: Change the AST walk to inspect yaml.safe_load Call nodes anywhere in the module (ast.walk(tree) directly for Call nodes), not only inside FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef.

claim: scripts/pull_alpaca_fills.py's docstring says it is "fail-soft: an account whose creds aren't set is skipped with a warning, not a hard abort," feeding runtime_state/exchange_fills.sqlite -> /api/bot/pnl/exchange and the broker-truth cost sweep. Its _fetch_page (lines 85-96) treats ANY Alpaca API failure (auth error, rate limit, 5xx, or a network exception -- AlpacaClient._request never raises, it returns {"retCode": -1, ...} on a network exception) the same as a legitimate empty page, and the --all-alpaca-accounts loop (main():113-144) has no try/except around _pull_one_account, unlike its Bybit/IB siblings.
location: scripts/pull_alpaca_fills.py:85-96, 108-144; src/runtime/exchange_fills_alpaca.py:96-99 (if not activities: break cannot distinguish the two); src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py:455-476 (_request never raises on HTTP failure)
evidence: Read src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py:455-476 confirming _request returns a synthetic error dict rather than raising on network failure. Contrast scripts/pull_exchange_fills.py:184-224, which wraps each account in try/except, tracks ok/failed/skipped separately, and exits 1 on any account failure -- the fix already shipped for BL-20260807-BYBIT-DEMO-FILLS-NEVER-PULLED (per docs/claude/system-actions.md), and mirrored in scripts/pull_exchange_funding.py:134-163 and scripts/pull_ib_executions.py's explicit IBReadError distinction. tests/test_exchange_fills_alpaca.py only covers the missing-creds skip path (test_all_alpaca_loop_skips_missing_creds, test_all_alpaca_all_missing_returns_2) -- no test for an API-failure-vs-empty-window distinction.
expected: An Alpaca API failure on a pull run should be distinguishable from a genuine no-fills window (via a non-zero exit code and/or a distinct failed-vs-ok account count), matching the already-fixed Bybit/IB pullers.
actual: A real Alpaca outage on alpaca_live/alpaca_portfolio (both real-money accounts) renders identically to "no fills today": candidates=0 inserted=0, exit code 0, ok count incremented, no signal that the pull did not actually happen.
population: 1 of 4 broker pullers (pull_alpaca_fills.py) lacks the fix; the other 3 (pull_exchange_fills.py, pull_exchange_funding.py, pull_ib_executions.py) already have it. Affects the 2 real-money Alpaca accounts (alpaca_live, alpaca_portfolio).
detector: Test mirroring tests for pull_exchange_fills.py's failure path: mock AlpacaClient._request to return a retCode!=0 error and assert the puller distinguishes it (non-zero exit / failed-count) from a mocked genuine empty page.
proposed_fix: Wrap each account in pull_alpaca_fills.py's --all-alpaca-accounts loop in try/except (mirroring pull_exchange_fills.py:184-224), track ok/failed/skipped separately, and make _fetch_page raise or return a distinguishable sentinel on API failure rather than the same [] as a legitimate empty page.

claim: scripts/run_smoke_once.sh's run_step() captures `local rc=$?` (line ~38) to log "STEP N : exit $rc", but any assignment via `local` clobbers $? before it can be read -- a well-known bash pitfall -- so the captured rc is (near-)always 0 regardless of the actual python exit code.
evidence: Read the function; confirmed OVERALL's actual pass/fail accounting keys off `$?` at the call site via `||` short-circuit, not off this captured rc, so the bug is confined to the log line's printed value.
expected: The "STEP N : exit $rc" log line should print the real exit code of the preceding python invocation.
actual: The log line is unreliable/misleading (near-always prints "exit 0") even though pass/fail accounting for OVERALL is unaffected.
